policy_title: Defend human rights and civil liberties
stated: Defend the Human Rights Act, support continued direct access to ECHR rights, restore legal aid for public law cases, protect religious expression, and scrap the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act and Public Order Act.

source.quote: Elected Greens will: • Defend the Human Rights Act. • Support continued direct access to ECHR rights in the domestic courts. • Restore legal aid for public law cases so everybody can uphold their rights in court. • Protect the right to religious expression. • Scrap the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act, Public Order Act and other legislation that erodes the right to protest and to free expression.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly addresses the legal-rights framework (Human Rights Act, ECHR access), due process (restoring legal aid for public law cases), civil liberties (religious expression), and protest/free-expression rights (scrapping the PCSC Act 2022 and Public Order Act 2023, which created new protest offences and expanded police powers to restrict demonstrations) — the core indicators of O9.

Scrapping the PCSC Act removes provisions including mandatory minimum sentences for knife offences and enhanced stop-and-search powers, which directly bear on O5 indicators (crime rates, charge/conviction outcomes) — the mechanism is concrete even if contested.

Scrapping the PCSC Act and Public Order Act directly removes state-imposed restrictions on protest, expression and movement; defending the HRA/ECHR and restoring legal aid for public law cases collectively expands individuals' ability to resist state coercion — all core O10 indicators.

membership_note: Two clear bearings: O10 (liberty/free speech) and O9 (equal treatment/due process). A tradeoff check on O5 was considered — scrapping the PCSC/Public Order Acts removes some protest-policing powers — but the concrete mechanism linking those specific provisions to material changes in crime rates or national security does not clear the non-negligible bar; the primary effect remains on liberty, not safety. No fiscal impact large enough to move O12 materially.
